temperature, different time: thickness decides how long the heat takes to reach the middle. Size Air fryer Oven Half cobs or small ears 400°F / 205°C · 10 min 425°F / 220°C · 13 min Medium cobs, halved to fit 400°F / 205°C · 12 min 425°F / 220°C · 16 min Large, thick cobs, halved 400°F / 205°C · 15 min 425°F / 220°C · 20 min Why the kernels go dry and wrinkled Boiled corn sits in water, so it can only get wetter. In an air fryer the opposite happens: hot, moving air pulls water out of every exposed kernel, and a bare cob left too long ends up shrivelled, chewy and pale. A coat of fat is what protects it. Butter or oil seals the kernels so they heat through and turn juicy, while the fat browns in spots for that roasted, grilled flavour. Size and fit matter too. Most full cobs are longer than a 5 qt basket, and a cob jammed in at an angle touches the sides, steams at the ends and blocks the air. Halve any cob longer than the basket so the pieces lie flat in one layer. Worked example: four ears of corn Four medium ears, husked, halved and brushed with melted butter and salt. Preheat 4 minutes, lay the halves in one layer and cook at 400°F for 12 minutes, turning them at 6. Small ears or short halves take about 10 minutes, and large, thick cobs about 15. Roasted on a tray in a conventional oven, the same corn takes 425°F for around 16 minutes. How to tell it is done The kernels should be bright yellow, plump and shiny, with a few golden-brown spots. Press one with a fingernail: it should pop with juice. Dull, dented kernels mean the corn dried out from too long or too little fat. Before it goes in Remove the husk and silk completely. Cut each cob with a heavy knife, rocking it through the core rather than sawing. Brush with butter or oil all round, and season after cooking if you are using a spice mix that burns. Smoked paprika, chilli and grated parmesan all work well tossed over the hot corn with a little more butter. Very fresh, sweet corn needs the shorter time; older, starchy cobs from the end of the season take a little longer to turn tender. About 12 minutes at 400°F for medium cobs, turned at 6. Small ears take around 10 minutes and large ones around 15. Do I need to cut corn to fit the air fryer? Usually, yes. Halve any cob longer than the basket so it lies flat; jammed-in cobs cook unevenly. Can I cook corn in the husk? You can, but it steams instead of roasting and the dry husk can scorch. Husked and buttered gives the best result. Can I air fry frozen corn on the cob? Yes, from frozen. Add a few minutes and brush with butter halfway, once the ice has gone. What is the oven equivalent? 425°F for around 16 minutes on a tray in a conventional oven, turned once.
